questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: The pituitary gland is historically designated in endocrine physiology as the:
questions.exp: The pituitary gland is designated as the master gland of endocrine. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: The anterior pituitary gland arises embryologically as an upgrowth from the roof of the ___.
questions.exp: The anterior pituitary originates as an upgrowth from the roof of the oral ectoderm forming Rathke's pouch. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: Match the pituitary lobe to its embryological origin — 1) Anterior pituitary 2) Posterior pituitary … A) Upgrowth from roof of oral ectoderm (Rathke's pouch) B) Downgrowth from floor of third ventricle (Neurohypophysis)
questions.exp: The anterior pituitary arises from oral ectoderm (Rathke's pouch) while the posterior pituitary develops as a downgrowth from the floor of the third ventricle. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: The most common etiology of congenital hypopituitarism is:
questions.exp: The most common cause of congenital hypopituitarism is pituitary dysplasia. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: Assess the statements on congenital hypopituitarism: I Only the anterior pituitary is typically involved in pituitary dysplasia. II Posterior pituitary function is routinely lost.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.exp: In congenital hypopituitarism secondary to pituitary dysplasia, only the anterior pituitary is involved. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: Which transcription factor mutation represents the most important molecular defect in congenital hypopituitarism?
questions.exp: Prop-1 mutation is the most important transcription factor defect underlying congenital hypopituitarism. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: A newborn infant presents with a solitary central maxillary incisor and midline facial cleft. Defective midline migration of cells during development from which embryological site explains this presentation?
questions.exp: Rathke's pouch cells migrate from the nasopharynx to the brain; defects in midline migration lead to craniofacial anomalies like single central incisors, bifid uvula, and cleft lip. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: Identify the anomaly that is NOT part of the midline craniofacial defects linked with Rathke's pouch migratory failure:
questions.exp: Midline craniofacial defects resulting from abnormal migration of Rathke's pouch cells include single central incisors, bifid uvula, and cleft lip, but not mandibular prognathism. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: What is the normal baseline weight of the adult human pituitary gland?
questions.exp: The pituitary gland normally weighs 600 mg. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: During normal pregnancy, the human pituitary gland undergoes physiological hyperplasia and enlarges to a weight of ___.
questions.exp: During pregnancy the pituitary gland enlarges from 600 mg to 1 gm. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: A 28-year-old woman suffers massive postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) during delivery. Compromised blood supply to her hypertrophied gland leads to ischemic necrosis, termed:
questions.exp: Severe blood loss from postpartum hemorrhage compromises blood supply to the enlarged gestational pituitary, resulting in Sheehan syndrome. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland
questions.q: Match the physiological state of the pituitary gland to its corresponding weight — 1) Baseline non-pregnant weight 2) Enlarged weight in pregnancy … A) 600 mg B) 1 gm
questions.exp: The pituitary gland weighs 600 mg at baseline and increases to 1 gm during pregnancy. (Book p936)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: Match the anterior pituitary cell type to its relative percentage — 1) Somatotrophs 2) Corticotrophs 3) Gonadotrophs 4) Thyrotrophs … A) 50% B) 15% C) 10% D) 5%
questions.exp: Somatotrophs account for 50%, corticotrophs 15%, lactotrophs 15%, gonadotrophs 10%, and thyrotrophs 5% of anterior pituitary cells. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: The earliest cells to appear during anterior pituitary development in the 6th embryonic week are:
questions.exp: Corticotrophs are the earliest cells to appear, emerging by the 6th week of embryonic life. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: The last anterior pituitary cell type to appear during ontogeny (emerging between 12 and 24 weeks) is the ___.
questions.exp: Lactotrophs are the last anterior pituitary cells to appear, emerging between 12 and 24 weeks. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: Match the twin hormones to their exact amino acid length — 1) Growth hormone (GH) 2) Prolactin (PRL) … A) 191 amino acids B) 199 amino acids
questions.exp: Growth hormone contains 191 amino acids while prolactin contains 199 amino acids. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: Assess the shared characteristics of GH and prolactin: I Both are acidophilic polypeptide hormones signaling via the JAK-STAT pathway. II Both cell lineages are located in the lateral portion of the gland.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Both GH and prolactin are acidophilic polypeptides signaling via the JAK-STAT pathway and reside in the lateral portion of the pituitary, predisposing them to ischemia. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: What proportion of GH-secreting pituitary adenomas also express lactotrophs?
questions.exp: GH-secreting adenomas co-express lactotrophs in 20% of cases as somatomammotrophic tumors. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: Why is clinically profound hypothyroidism not typically observed in isolated hypopituitarism?
opts: Reverse T3 converts spontaneously into bioactive free thyroxine
Parathyroid hormone exerts secondary agonism on follicular TSH receptors
20% of thyroid hormone is produced autonomously by the thyroid gland itself
Peripheral deiodinases increase activity ten-fold in TSH absence
questions.exp: Twenty percent of thyroid hormone is produced autonomously by the gland itself independent of TSH. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: An endocrine pathologist examines an anterior pituitary specimen. The corticotroph cells exhibit the largest secretory granules measuring:
questions.exp: Corticotroph secretory granules are the largest in the anterior pituitary, measuring 400 to 550 nm. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: Which peptide is NOT a direct cleavage derivative of pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)?
questions.exp: POMC is cleaved into ACTH, MSH, and beta-lipotrophin; oxytocin is a neurohypophyseal nonapeptide. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: Beta-lipotrophin is cleaved to produce endorphins, which function as endogenous analgesics by blocking:
questions.exp: Endorphins derived from beta-lipotrophin act as natural painkillers by blocking mu opioid receptors. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: Match the transcription factor to its developmental role — 1) Prop-1 2) Pit-1 3) T-pit 4) GATA-2 … A) Most common cause of congenital hypopituitarism B) Second most common cause of congenital hypopituitarism C) Corticotroph cell development D) Gonadotroph differentiation via SF-1/DAX-1
questions.exp: Prop-1 is the most common cause of congenital hypopituitarism, Pit-1 is the 2nd most common, T-pit directs corticotrophs, and GATA-2 directs gonadotrophs via SF-1/DAX-1. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: Under the DOSE happiness hormones mnemonic, which factor is NOT listed as increasing endorphin levels?
questions.exp: Endorphins increase with increased heart rate, waking up early, and dark chocolate; prolonged sleep deprivation is not listed. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Anterior pituitary cell lineages and hormones
questions.q: The glycoprotein hormones sharing an identical alpha subunit secreted by the anterior pituitary are TSH, FSH, and ___.
questions.exp: The glycoprotein alpha hormones are TSH, FSH, and LH; GH, PRL, and POMC are polypeptide hormones. (Book p937)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Which arterial vessel joins the capillary plexus at the median eminence to form the hypothalamo-hypophysial portal system?
questions.exp: The superior hypophyseal artery joins the median eminence to form the hypothalamo-hypophysial portal system supplying the anterior lobe. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: The sole anterior pituitary hormone maintained under tonic negative hypothalamic inhibition by dopamine is ___.
questions.exp: Prolactin is under dominant tonic negative hypothalamic inhibition mediated by prolactin inhibitory factor (PRIF / dopamine). (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Match the hypothalamic releasing factor to its anterior pituitary target — 1) CRH 2) TRH 3) GnRH 4) GHRH … A) Corticotrophs (ACTH) B) Thyrotrophs (TSH) C) Gonadotrophs (FSH/LH) D) Somatotrophs (GH)
questions.exp: CRH, TRH, GnRH, and GHRH exert stimulatory influence over corticotrophs, thyrotrophs, gonadotrophs, and somatotrophs respectively. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: A neuroscientist traces the synthesis of antidiuretic hormone. Magnocellular neurons in which hypothalamic nuclei produce pro-vasopressin?
questions.exp: Magnocellular neurons within the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei produce pro-vasopressin. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Which molecule is NOT a cleavage product of pro-vasopressin transported down the pituitary stalk?
questions.exp: Pro-vasopressin cleaves into ADH, neurophysin, and copeptin; oxytocin is a distinct nonapeptide synthesized separately. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Assess the vascular supply of the pituitary gland: I The anterior lobe receives regulatory hormones through long portal vessels derived from the superior hypophyseal artery. II The posterior lobe receives direct arterial branches from the inferior hypophyseal artery.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: The anterior lobe receives portal blood via the superior hypophyseal artery, whereas the posterior pituitary is supplied directly by the inferior hypophyseal artery. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: A 54-year-old woman with metastatic breast adenocarcinoma develops acute central diabetes insipidus. Metastatic emboli reached her posterior pituitary directly through which vessel?
questions.exp: Breast carcinoma metastases can directly seed the posterior pituitary gland via the inferior hypophyseal artery. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Oxytocin is synthesized within hypothalamic magnocellular neurons and stored within the:
questions.exp: Oxytocin is synthesized in the hypothalamus and stored in the posterior pituitary. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Dopamine reaches the anterior pituitary lactotrophs via the ___ pathway to suppress prolactin secretion.
questions.exp: Dopamine acts as prolactin inhibitory factor via the tubero-infundibular pathway. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Match the pituitary lobe to its primary vascular route — 1) Anterior pituitary 2) Posterior pituitary … A) Hypothalamo-hypophysial portal system (Superior hypophyseal artery) B) Direct systemic arterial supply (Inferior hypophyseal artery)
questions.exp: The anterior pituitary is supplied by the portal system from the superior hypophyseal artery, while the posterior lobe receives direct systemic blood via the inferior hypophyseal artery. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Assess the hypothalamic control of anterior pituitary secretion: I Somatostatin exerts an inhibitory influence on growth hormone release. II Prolactin secretion increases when the pituitary stalk is sectioned.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Somatostatin inhibits GH secretion; sectioning the stalk interrupts dopamine delivery, causing prolactin hypersecretion. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Hypothalamic-pituitary vascular and neural connections
questions.q: Which cleavage marker of pro-vasopressin serves as an equimolar, stable surrogate for ADH release?
questions.exp: Copeptin is cleaved from pro-vasopressin alongside ADH and neurophysin. (Book p938)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: Which anatomical structure lies immediately posterior and inferior to the sella turcica, providing the standard surgical corridor for pituitary adenomas?
questions.exp: The sphenoid sinus lies posterior/inferior to the sella and allows the transsphenoidal surgical approach. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: The dural reflection forming the roof of the hypophyseal fossa is the ___; injury to it can cause CSF rhinorrhea and empty sella syndrome.
questions.exp: The diaphragma sellae forms the dural roof of the sella; injury leads to CSF leaks and empty sella syndrome. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: A 45-year-old male with a large pituitary macroadenoma expanding laterally into the cavernous sinus presents with acute diplopia and isolated left lateral rectus palsy. Which cranial nerve is involved first?
questions.exp: Lateral expansion of a pituitary tumor into the cavernous sinus involves the sixth cranial nerve (abducent nerve) first, causing lateral rectus palsy. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: Which neural or vascular structure does NOT traverse the cavernous sinus adjacent to the pituitary fossa?
questions.exp: The cavernous sinus contains the internal carotid artery, CN III, CN IV, CN VI, V1, and V2; V3 passes through the foramen ovale outside the sinus. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: Match the sellar boundary to its primary related structure — 1) Lateral relation 2) Inferior/posterior approach 3) Ventral/superior dural roof … A) Cavernous sinus B) Sphenoid sinus C) Diaphragma sellae
questions.exp: The cavernous sinus lies laterally, the sphenoid sinus lies inferiorly/posteriorly, and the diaphragma sellae forms the roof. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: On non-contrast T1-weighted coronal and sagittal MRI, the normal pituitary gland appears:
questions.exp: On T1 MRI (coronal, sagittal, and without contrast), the normal pituitary appears isointense. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: Assess the contrast enhancement patterns of the pituitary gland: I The normal pituitary demonstrates uniform avid gadolinium enhancement. II A pituitary microadenoma typically exhibits delayed or non-uniform enhancement due to lower capillary vascularity.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Normal pituitary shows uniform contrast uptake, whereas adenomas demonstrate less vascularity and do not take up contrast uniformly. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: A neuroradiologist evaluates a sagittal T1 MRI of a 22-year-old male with severe polyuria and polydipsia. Absence of the normal hyperintense posterior pituitary 'bright spot' is diagnostic of:
questions.exp: Absence of the normal posterior pituitary T1 bright spot is diagnostic of central diabetes insipidus in 80% of cases. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: The normal T1-weighted sagittal MRI 'bright spot' in the posterior sella represents stored vasopressin-neurophysin granules in the ___ pituitary.
questions.exp: The normal bright spot on sagittal T1 MRI represents stored neurosecretory granules in the posterior pituitary. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: Match the MRI appearance on T1 imaging to the pathological condition — 1) Normal posterior lobe bright spot absent 2) Hypoenhancing focal sellar lesion 3) Diffuse uniform gadolinium uptake … A) Central diabetes insipidus (80%) B) Pituitary adenoma C) Normal anterior pituitary gland
questions.exp: Absence of bright spot indicates central DI; focal hypoenhancement indicates adenoma; uniform contrast uptake indicates normal gland. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: Which trigeminal nerve divisions traverse the cavernous sinus along its lateral dural wall?
questions.exp: The lateral wall of the cavernous sinus contains the ophthalmic (V1) and maxillary (V2) divisions of the trigeminal nerve. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI
questions.q: Assess the clinical implications of diaphragmatic injury: I A tear in the diaphragma sellae can cause CSF leakage. II Chronic CSF pressure through the defect can lead to empty sella syndrome.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Injury to the diaphragma sellae permits CSF leakage and can progress to empty sella syndrome. (Book p939)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: Match the pituitary adenoma classification to its size criterion — 1) Microadenoma 2) Macroadenoma … A) Less than 1 cm B) Greater than 1 cm
questions.exp: Microadenomas are < 1 cm while macroadenomas are > 1 cm in diameter. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: Compression of the infundibulum by an expanding macroadenoma produces hyperprolactinemia through the ___ effect.
questions.exp: Pituitary stalk compression disrupts dopamine transit, resulting in the stalk effect with hyperprolactinemia. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: What two primary mechanisms mediate the clinical consequences of a non-functioning pituitary adenoma?
opts: Direct cortical invasion and CSF seeding
questions.exp: Non-functioning pituitary adenomas cause clinical manifestations via stalk effect and mass effect. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: Assess the effects of functioning pituitary adenomas: I Functioning adenomas can produce mass effect resulting in increased intracranial tension. II Functioning adenomas produce specific hormonal dysfunction in addition to potential stalk effect.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.exp: Functioning adenomas produce hormonal dysfunction, mass effect with increased intracranial tension, and stalk effect. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: A 52-year-old woman is discovered to have a 2.4 cm sellar lesion that stains negative for all anterior pituitary hormones. Her serum prolactin is 65 ug/L. The mild prolactin elevation is best explained by:
opts: Stalk effect from dopamine tract disruption
questions.exp: Non-functioning macroadenomas compress the pituitary stalk, blocking dopamine delivery to lactotrophs and causing mild hyperprolactinemia (stalk effect). (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: Mass effect from suprasellar extension of a macroadenoma classically produces:
opts: Isolated lower motor neuron facial weakness
questions.exp: Mass effect from an expanding pituitary adenoma elevates intracranial tension leading to headaches and visual symptoms. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: Which feature is NOT typically associated with non-functioning pituitary macroadenomas?
opts: Increased intracranial tension from mass effect
questions.exp: Non-functioning adenomas do not hypersecrete hormones; they cause hypopituitarism, stalk effect, and mass effect. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: Match the adenoma consequence to its pathophysiologic manifestation — 1) Stalk effect 2) Mass effect 3) Functioning adenoma … A) Hypopituitarism with mild hyperprolactinemia B) Increased intracranial tension C) Autonomous hormone overproduction
questions.exp: Stalk effect leads to hypopituitarism and prolactinemia; mass effect increases intracranial tension; functioning tumors cause hormonal dysfunction. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: A pituitary adenoma measuring 0.7 cm on coronal MRI is designated as a ___.
questions.exp: An adenoma under 1 cm is categorized as a microadenoma. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: Involvement of the pituitary stalk by a large sellar tumor can directly cause hypopituitarism and:
questions.exp: Stalk effect causes hypopituitarism and hyperprolactinemia due to loss of tonic dopamine inhibition. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: Assess the characteristics of pituitary mass lesions: I Non-functioning adenomas frequently go unnoticed until visual loss or mass effects develop. II Stalk compression impairs anterior pituitary trophic stimulation while increasing prolactin.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Non-functioning adenomas present late with mass effect; stalk interruption reduces trophic hormones but raises prolactin. (Book p940)

questions.sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects
questions.q: A 38-year-old man presents with progressive bitemporal visual field deficits and severe headaches. MRI reveals a 3.2 cm suprasellar lesion compressing the optic chiasm and infundibulum. This tumor is classified as a:
questions.exp: Any pituitary adenoma exceeding 1 cm in diameter is classified as a macroadenoma. (Book p940)
